planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; one of the oldest plain-white selections of the species, grown alongside the pink 'Rose Queen' and violet 'Violet Queen' as part of the same long-cultivated color range.

directions: Album is a long-cultivated, plain white-flowered selection of the Japanese and Korean species Epimedium grandiflorum, grown for its simple, clean color rather than the bicolor spurs seen in many other longspur barrenwort cultivars. Heart-shaped compound leaflets emerge tinged in copper-bronze in early spring before settling to green, forming a quiet backdrop for the small sprays of pure white, four-spurred flowers that open on wiry stems in mid-spring. Like other forms of the species, it spreads gradually by rhizome into a dense, weed-suppressing patch and tolerates the dry, root-filled shade beneath mature deciduous trees far better than most groundcovers once established. Shear or comb out tattered winter foliage in late winter so the modest spring flower display is not obscured.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; the violet-purple counterpart to the pink 'Rose Queen' and white 'White Queen' selections, rounding out the classic 'Queen' strain of this species.

directions: Violet Queen is a classic cultivar of the Japanese and Korean species Epimedium grandiflorum, valued for flowers in a richer violet-purple than the typical pink or white forms of the species, carried in airy sprays with four long, elegant spurs per bloom. Compound, heart-shaped leaflets emerge bronze-tinted in spring before maturing to green, then take on rust-bronze winter tones on the semi-evergreen foliage in milder climates. It spreads slowly by rhizome into a dense, weed-suppressing mat and shares the species' notable tolerance for dry, root-filled shade beneath established deciduous trees. Cut back or comb out old foliage in late winter before new growth begins, so the spring flower display is fully visible.
